habitat: Wikipedia says it is abundant south of the Sahel, partial in East Africa, and absent in southern Africa. That last clause conflicts with its place on the Kruger list, so no status was taken from it. The plumage was not described.
summary: Newman has no page. Wikipedia names the bird and its range and does not describe the plumage, so the marks were left empty. The sentence that it is absent in southern Africa was not used to set status, because the species is on the Kruger list. The Kemp code RB was left unchanged.

similar.note: Newman separates Emerald-spotted Wood Dove by its all-dark reddish bill, greyer upperparts and green wing-spots, seen in good light.

sources.title: The Atlas of Southern African Birds, Vol. 1 (Bluespotted Dove)

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^3=8 mature individuals (resident breeder); paper interval half–double → 4–16.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

viewNotes.note: Plumage was not described in the texts used.
The upperwing was not described. Newman says the wood-dove flight pattern is not by itself diagnostic.

calls.description: Wikipedia does not describe the call. The file is grade A from Katama, Uganda. The filename is Turtur_afer_Blue-spotted_Wood-Dove.

research.note: No Kruger photograph was found under an allowed licence. A side photograph from Mopani is stored. Newman has no usable length for this species in the sources used here, and Wikipedia gives no total length, so size is omitted. Population figures were left unchanged. SABAP1 does not describe residency or movements, so status stays omitted.
